newsitem.title: CANADA: Rio Algom discovers Chilean copper.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom discovers Chilean copper.

text.p: Rio Algom Ltd said on Thursday it discovered a major copper deposit in northern Chile.
The find, called the Spence deposit, is about 140 kilometers northeast of Antofagasta on the highway to Calama on claims held by Rio Algom's wholly owned Compania Minera Riochilex S.A.
A recent drilling program of more than 24,000 metres outlined an inferred resource of about 350 million tonnes averaging one percent copper, Rio Algom said.
The deposit also contained minor values in silver and molybdenum.
Rio said that drilling so far suggested the deposit would suit an open pit mine and conventional metallurgical treatment.
The company has drilled 81 vertical holes spaced at 200 metres and six angle holes to an average depth of 280 metres.

A second drill program and preliminary metallurgical testing would start on the deposit this month to upgrade the resource into proven and probable reserves and prepare for a feasibility study to start in the second half of 1997, Rio Algom said.

The deposit "has the potential to produce copper at a rate greater than our very successful Cerro Colorado mine which will reach a level of 220 million pounds of copper per annum in 1998," Rio Algom chairman Gordon Gray said in a statement.
